text.p: Headlines from major national newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
EL PAIS
- Economy Minister Rodrigo Rato demands wage moderation to join single European currency.

- Government distances itself from Deputy Prime Minister Francisco Alvarez Cascos' accusations that former Socialist prime minister Felipe Gonzalez orchestrated death squad campaign against Basque separatists.
EL MUNDO
- Socialist Workers' Party (PSOE) asks Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar to say whether he supports Cascos' accusations.
- Government removes financing of public sector companies from budget.

- Defence Ministry exempts former head of military intelligence General Emilio Alonso Manglano from any wrong-doing and says former spy Colonel Juan Alberto Perote is only culprit in case of covert filming of top officials in luxury chalet rented by intelligence service.
DIARIO 16
- Madrid mayor Jose Maria Alvarez de Manzano sanctioned destruction of city's arab wall in renovation works.
- Rato trusts budget will guarantee everything -- growth, employment, interest rates, inflation, solidarity and meeting Maastricht criteria.
- Cascos unleashes rhetorical fury of Socialists.
ABC
- Theatre honours writer Antonio Buero Vallejo on his 80th birthday.
CINCO DIAS
- State sweeps 525 billion pesetas deficit under the carpet by excluding aid to public companies from 1997 budget.
- Popular Party (PP) government plans to launch high-speed train link between Madrid and Valladolid.
- Another monopoly broken: Petrogal sells butane gas in cannisters.
- Telefonica doesn't charge for failed connections on Infovia Internet service.
EXPANSION
- Rato says budget will allow cut in interest rates.
- Government fixes privatisation of Retevision for May 1997.
- Auditors detect hereditary deficit of 2.4 billion pesetas at Banco Credipas.
- Juan Fernandez-Armesto will be next head of stock exchange commission CNMV.
- Argentaria ceases partnership with Grupo Ferrovial by selling 10 percent of Autopista del Sol to Unicaja.
GACETA DE LOS NEGOCIOS
- Rato pledges strict compliance with budget.
